# SK2003 — Review exact equality of floating-point arithmetic

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

Exact equality or inequality directly compares a computed float or double arithmetic result.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

Binary floating-point arithmetic rounds its results. A mathematical equality can therefore differ from exact machine equality. An appropriate tolerance depends on the domain and scale; the rule reports the comparison without inventing an epsilon or replacing it with Equals.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
bool M(double x, double y, double expected) => x + y == expected;
```

Write:

```csharp
// Choose a domain-appropriate comparison, or retain intentional exact equality with a scoped suppression.
```

## When it does not fire

The initial scope requires a direct built-in addition, subtraction, multiplication, division or remainder operand of a built-in, non-lifted float/double == or != comparison. Plain variable comparisons, property change guards, decimal/integral arithmetic, custom operators, constant-folded comparisons, and comparisons against constant zero, NaN or infinity are excluded. Source constant dependencies must stay in the same file, including transitive initializers. It does not trace earlier arithmetic through variables or method calls. Exact floating-point contracts may be intentional and can require suppression; no automatic fix is offered.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2003.severity`
